newsitem.title: FRANCE: Airbus partners sign restructuring deal.
newsitem.headline: Airbus partners sign restructuring deal.

text.p: Aircraft manfacturer Airbus Industrie said on Monday its four European partners had signed a memorandum of understanding to restructure Airbus into a limited liability company by 1999.

Toulouse-based Airbus is currently a partnership between French state-owned Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace(DASA), and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA(CASA) of Spain.
"The establishment of Airbus Industrie as a single corporate entity (SCE) is an important initial step in the consolidation of the aerospace industry within Europe," Airbus said.

The SCE will have a single management structure which should add control of engineering, testing, production, procurement and customer service to Airbus's current responsibilities for marketing, sales and product support, it said in a statement.

"Transfer of assets associated with these functions... will depend on how far the assets are essential for the described functions and their detailed valuation, to be completed by the end of 1997," it said.
Airbus said the agreement, first announced in preliminary form in early January, was signed on Monday.
The four partners decided last July to turn Airbus into a corporation to streamline decision-making and production.
These restrucuturing plans took on a more urgent tone after Boeing and McDonnell Douglas said last month they would merge and form a civil and military giant with nearly $50 billion in annual sales.
